finding_summary: Phase 1: ramps mmtc offered load at a wide-open ceiling through 9 multipliers (52-80x) bracketing the ~59x estimate interpolated from M44-A's own committed demand curve, recording real per-UE avg_prbs_dl demand at each via the same method M44-A itself used (m44_scarcity_probe.py's launch_ramped_traffic/poll_demand, unmodified).

52x=6.73PRB, 55x=6.93, 58x=7.33, 60x=7.40, 62x=7.53, 65x=9.87(max=38, noisy outlier), 70x=8.60, 75x=8.80, 80x=9.87(max=12). Chose 80x/4000Kbps: closest mean to urllc's own M44-D reference (mean=10.20,max=13.00) with a comparable, well-behaved max/mean ratio, avoiding 65x's outlier.

column5: First launch of the phase-2 cold-start sweep at 80x/4000Kbps used the script's default output dir, which is shared per-slice regardless of offered load -- would have appended the new 4000Kbps data into the SAME trajectory_mmtc_ceil{N}.jsonl files as E1's already-committed 2500Kbps data for ceilings 5-9, conflating two different offered-load datasets in one file. column10: Gate PASS and buffer confirmed 0.0% before traffic at all 6 runs. Zero new_max_retx_events across all 48 samples.

finding_summary: ceiling=5 (floor): 2129.8+/-20.4Kbps served, 47.28+/-0.57% loss, 46.74+/-0.67% RLC rejected -- severe, bounded degradation. ceiling=6: 2921.7+/-9.9Kbps, 27.02+/-0.84% loss, 24.85+/-0.53% rejected. ceiling=7: 2904.8+/-80.8Kbps, 27.02+/-0.71% loss, 25.81+/-2.31% rejected -- statistically indistinguishable from ceiling=6. ceiling=8/9/10: full health, 0%/0% throughout, statistically indistinguishable from each other. Every degraded ceiling showed the same delayed-onset shape as urllc's own M44-D 6-PRB trajectory (clean for ~55-75s, then settling into a bounded degraded state by ~100s), reconfirming the >=120s hold requirement.

A real, graded (non-binary) band exists for mmtc at 4000Kbps/80x: full health (8-10 PRB) / moderate bounded degradation (6-7 PRB, the two statistically indistinguishable from each other) / severe bounded degradation (5 PRB, the floor). BUT: reaching this regime required driving mmtc at 80x its own native PEAK burst rate (~320x its true average rate) as a SUSTAINED CONTINUOUS stream, not its native bursty 2s-on/6s-off pattern -- explicitly flagged as atypical, not recognizably mMTC-like traffic. Compared to urllc's ~3600Kbps/12x-native regime: absolute Kbps is close (4000 vs 3600) but the RELATIVE departure from each slice's own native character is categorically larger for mmtc (80x peak / 320x average, vs urllc's 12x sustained) -- an open concern handed to E3's common-regime question, not resolved here. embb (E2) and the common-regime search (E3) have not been started.
